name: Jamaican Boiled Dumplings
assumptions: Yield estimated from typical Jamaican boiled dumpling recipes using 2 cups flour, which commonly serve 4 as a side dish.
Total time is sum of active prep (mixing, shaping ~15 min) and passive boiling (20 min max from instructions); excludes bringing pot to boil.
All-purpose flour confirmed as wheat-based, making it not gluten-free.
No animal products, dairy, eggs, or nuts listed, supporting vegan/vegetarian/dairy-free.
Water and salt for boiling are partially discarded and not primary allergens.
instructions:
Instructions
 
In a large pot, bring water and salt to a boil to boil the dumplings.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the all-purpose flour and salt, stirring to distribute the salt evenly throughout the flour. Gradually add water to the flour mixture, mixing with your hands until a dough forms.
Divide the dough into equal-sized pieces, rolling each into a smooth ball. Flatten each ball slightly with the palm of your hand to form a round, circular dumpling. It should look like a thick disk.
Carefully drop the dumplings into the boiling water, one at a time, ensuring that they don't stick together. You can use a wooden spoon to stir the dumplings in the water.
Boil the dumplings for 15-20 minutes, or until they are cooked through and have risen to the surface of the water. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the cooked dumplings from the pot, allowing any excess water to drain.
Serve with your favorite recipes.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.assumptions: 8 cups water = 1920 g (standard density 1 g/ml; used for boiling and discarded after cooking)

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.assumptions: 1/2 tablespoon table salt = 9 g (salt contributes negligible macros when dissolved and mostly discarded with boiling water)

ingredients.name: All purpose flour
ingredients.assumptions: 2 cups all-purpose flour = 250 g (standard volume-to-weight conversion for unsifted AP flour; fully incorporated into final edible dumplings)

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.assumptions: 1 teaspoon table salt = 5 g (salt contributes negligible macros; remains in the cooked dumplings)

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.assumptions: 1/2 cup water = 120 g (standard density 1 g/ml; fully absorbed into dough and remains in final edible dumplings)
